phases.name: Slice 01: A session for every game (walking skeleton)
phases.description: The table issues a session for every game and refuses a signing without one (flip 1); one row per game; sessions last 2 hours; the browser asks for its session as each game starts and signs with it. Ends with slice 01's smoke steps, local edges and owner docs.

steps.name: The session signer, and the token rule first
criteria: createSessionSigner(secret) signs v1.{seed}.{issuedAt} with HMAC-SHA256 as 43 base64url characters; gameId(seed) is the first 32 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the seed's text.
verify returns false, never throws, for any changed field, a token from another secret, a 42- or 44-character token, or a session of the wrong shape.
readSessionSecret returns the 32 bytes only for canonical base64 of exactly 32 bytes (44 characters that re-encode to themselves), and null for anything else.
The layering spec's token rule finds no test-clock, test-board, __test or TEST_SECRET in src/** or netlify/**, comments included, and reports each one planted.
No scenario is enabled and nothing calls the signer yet: the unit and in-memory projects pass as before.
steps.scenario_name: any changed field of a session fails verify, and a token from another secret never verifies (unit) | tokens of 42 and 44 characters verify false and never throw (unit) | readSessionSecret takes canonical base64 of exactly 32 bytes, and nothing else (unit) | no test-only name (test-clock, test-board, __test, TEST_SECRET) appears in src or netlify, comments included (unit)
steps.implementation_notes: DISTILL's enable order, slice 01 step 1, its first two items, split out as a precursor so that the walking-skeleton commit (01-02) is the flip itself. THE TOKEN RULE comes first (DISTILL's unit item 'before E1', the platform review's PL-2): a text scan in tests/unit/layering.spec.js, read like the import scan (it can over-report, never miss): test-clock, test-board, __test and TEST_SECRET appear nowhere in src/** or netlify/**, comments included. DISTILL already reworded the one comment that named a test board. scripts/ and tests/ are outside it. THE SIGNER, netlify/scores/sessions.mjs (DDD-R2, C1), with node:crypto only: readSessionSecret(value) returns the 32 bytes for a value of 44 characters matching ^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{43}=$ that decodes to 32 bytes and re-encodes to the same text (so no non-zero padding bits), and null for anything else (DEVOPS's 'For DELIVER' item 2). createSessionSigner(secret) returns { sign(seed, issuedAt) -> token, verify(session) -> boolean, gameId(seed) -> 32 hex }, each usable detached, since the handlers take them unbound (DDD-R1). The token is HMAC-SHA256 over `v1.{seed}.{issuedAt}`, base64url, 43 characters. verify checks the shape first (an object with exactly a 32-lowercase-hex seed, a safe-integer issuedAt and a 43-character base64url token), returns false on any mismatch, and only then compares two buffers of equal length with timingSafeEqual. Delete the file's `export const __SCAFFOLD__ = true` and its RED-scaffold comment. Nothing calls the signer yet: under TABLE_PROTOCOL BARE the leaderboard's harness builds none, and this feature's scenarios stay @pending (they now stop at the handler instead of the signer). Enables no scenario: test_file and scenario_name name the unit tests this step adds. steps.name: Walking skeleton: no signing without a session (flip 1)
criteria: A signature with no session is refused 400 session-required, with one log line that says nothing about the player, and the table is left as it was (the walking skeleton).

Each game start sends one POST /api/sessions for a fresh seed, whose rows refresh the table; its signing carries that game's session; the leaderboard's and typed-initials' suites stay green in three engines.

The Netlify entry serves both paths under one rate-limit rule and builds its signer from SCORES_SESSION_SECRET, or none (500 secret-missing); unit tests cover both kinds of secret, both paths and the config contract.
GET and the session request get a read-only { list }; handleSessions gets only { sign }, handleScores only { verify, gameId } and no newId, because a row's id is its game id.

Flip 1: TABLE_PROTOCOL is SESSION; leaderboard M2's 'can't file' scenario, its step and makeRowsItCantFile are deleted; the broken unit specs are rewritten; serve.mjs serves /api/sessions and, to test boards, POST /__test/rows.

steps.name: One game, one row on the table
criteria: A signing for a game whose row is on the table, with the same or another session, is 409 already-signed: its own key removed, and a reading taken meanwhile shows the row once.
If that removal fails, the answer is still 409, with one log line, scores.rejected already-signed with removed: false, and the key is left to pruning.
The ranking shows each game's first-signed key only; pruning removes a game's other keys first, then the lowest winners past 20, at most 5 deletes per signing (unit property).
A refused attempt doesn't use up its session; a game saved before a failed listing has signed; bursts of 2 to 5 never show two rows, and a signing sent ahead keeps its row.
Variants S5, S6 and S7 each fail the scenarios DISTILL names.

After its write and its listing, a signing keeps its key only if the listing shows no other well-formed key with its game id; otherwise it removes its own key and answers 409 already-signed, logged scores.rejected already-signed; if that removal fails it is still 409 with one log line carrying removed: false, and the key is left to pruning (a loser, so it never shows). steps.name: Each game asks for its session once, as it starts
criteria: Typed initials sign through the game's own session: 'Signing ALX…', then 'Signed ALX, #4.', the row marked as mine, and the signing carried the session the table gave that game.
